exposure: Oregon's hard-stop policy limiting early elective deliveries before 39 weeks of gestation
Oregon's hard-stop policy limiting early elective deliveries (before 39 weeks of gestation)
outcome: Rate of elective inductions at 37 or 38 weeks
Rate of elective cesarean deliveries at 37 or 38 weeks
cohort: 181,034 Term or postterm, cephalic, nonanomalous, singleton births in Oregon between 2008 and 2013
finding: Oregon's hard-stop policy was associated with a reduction in elective early-term deliveries, but did not improve maternal or neonatal outcomes, and was associated with an increase in chorioamnionitis.
mod_finding: Oregon's statewide policy to limit elective early-term delivery was associated with a reduction in elective early-term deliveries, including both inductions and cesarean deliveries.
